title: Introduce weighted premerge lanes and toolchain slimdown
author: Aisha Raman
release_notes: Adds weighted presubmit lanes to reduce overall CI cost and stops running full toolchain install on low-impact changes; backwards-compatible; no runtime changes.
description:
Summary: Introduce a lightweight presubmit orchestration layer that assigns weighted lanes to PRs based on a small impact heuristic (file globs, language touchpoints, and directory ownership). The goal is faster feedback for routine docs/config/small SDK changes while retaining full test coverage for high-impact code paths. Additionally, replace bloated test images with slimline per-language toolchain profiles and a two-stage cache priming so most presubmit jobs skip heavy package installs.

Motivation: CI spend and latency have been steadily growing; many PRs touch only README or docs and still wait for full toolchain installs. This causes long feedback loops and discourages small iterative changes. We need a low-risk way to: 1) reduce average presubmit time/cost, 2) prioritize critical lanes for high-confidence verification, and 3) keep the system transparent and auditable for SRE/SEC. ENG-2345 tracks the cost objectives; ENG-2399 tracks the slim image rollout.

What changed (high level): - Introduced presubmit-weighted router (ci/presubmit/router.ts) that computes a lane weight {fast, standard, full} from heuristics: changed file globs, manifest diffs, and owner hints. - Added declarative lane definitions (ci/presubmit/lanes.yaml) with thresholds for required checks and time budgets. - Implemented toolchain profiles (ci/toolchains/README.md + profiles/*) that describe minimal package sets for fast lanes and fuller sets for standard/full lanes. - Introduced image layering and two-stage cache priming in Dockerfiles to allow skip-install quickstart for fast lanes. - Added a lightweight telemetry ping for presubmit decisions (metrics only; no PII) and an audit log to trace why a PR ran a particular lane. - CI changes: GitHub Actions composable workflows updated to use conditional job paths and a new presubmit dispatcher step.

Commits (summary): - feat(presubmit): add presubmit router and lane heuristics (A. Raman) - feat(ci): lanes.yaml and dispatcher workflow (A. Raman) - chore(toolchain): introduce slimline python/node/rust profiles + base images (J. Kim) - ci: add cache-priming step and telemetry shim (M. Ortega) - fix(ci): permissions for audit-sink and secrets in dispatcher (P. Shah)

Files touched (representative): - ci/presubmit/router.ts - ci/presubmit/lanes.yaml - .github/workflows/presubmit-dispatch.yml - ci/toolchains/profiles/python-slim.Dockerfile - ci/toolchains/profiles/node-slim.Dockerfile - ci/toolchains/cache-priming.sh - tooling/presubmit-audit/README.md

Testing and CI: - Local unit tests for router heuristics with mocked file lists. - Integration harness (ci/integration/presubmit-sim) to simulate PR diffs and validate mapping counts. - GitHub Actions matrix validated across linux/ubuntu-22/macOS (reused existing runners). - Initial rollout gated behind a feature flag in presubmit router to allow canary on small number of repos. - CI status: first run failed due to runner permissions on the audit sink; fixed in follow-up commit and then all checks passed; final CI status: pass.

Rollout plan and migration notes: - Default behavior preserved: if dispatch feature flag is off, existing presubmit flow unchanged. - Gradual canary: enable feature flag for 10% of repos (internal config) for 48 hours, validate false positives and missed coverage. - Telemetry and audit logs will be reviewed daily for the first week; an automatic rollback policy is in place if flakiness > 5% in critical lanes. - No repo changes required; teams can opt-out per-repo via ci/presubmit/lanes.yaml override.

Review conversation (condensed): - Miguel O: "Router looks reasonable; can you add a short circuit for monorepo-wide breakages so we don't under-test large changes?" — Aisha: "Added threshold on number of touched files to force full lane (see lanes.yaml threshold_count)." - Priya S: "Audit logs need stricter access; remove secrets from telemetry payloads." — Aisha: "Telemetry is metrics-only; audit sink ACL tightened in fix commit." - Liam O'C: "Please add a changelog entry and a brief explainer doc for platform teams." — Aisha: "Added tooling/presubmit-audit/README.md and release notes." - QA: "Observed flaky node-slim image layer on ubuntu runner" — J. Kim: "Pinned node-builder base and added retry logic to cache-priming step." Approvals: Miguel, Priya, Liam approved after fixes.

CI checks summary: - unit-tests (linux): pass - integration-sim (matrix): pass - lint (typescript/python): pass - image-build (node/python): pass after retry - release/signing-checks: pass

Security & compliance: - No secrets transmitted by router; audit sink access restricted to infra SRE role. - Toolchain profiles documented and reviewed by security to ensure no unexpected network egress in fast lanes.

Why this is different from previous PRs: Rather than monolithic CI refactor or simply trimming deps, this PR introduces an orchestration layer that can assign presubmit intensity based on an explainable heuristic and per-repo policies. It pairs policy with concrete engineering work (slim images + cache priming) to realize latency/cost wins without sacrificing safety.

Metrics observed in canary (internal): - Median presubmit time reduced 42% for fast lane PRs. - Average CI CPU-minutes reduced 31% across canary repos. - No regressions in flakiness for full lanes during 48-hour canary.

Follow-ups (tracked in Linear): - ENG-2401: add waterfall visualizer in Console to show lane assignment per PR. - ENG-2412: expose per-team override UI in Console. - ENG-2420: expand heuristics to use owner labels and historical flaky-test signals.

Merge: squash+merge on 2026-02-23 after all approvals and CI green.

Checklist: [x] Tests added/updated [x] Docs updated (tooling/presubmit-audit/README.md) [x] Linear tickets linked [x] Security reviewed [x] Rollout plan included

If anything unexpected shows up in post-merge CI telemetry, revert is prepared (branch: rollback/presubmit-weighted-298765).
